name: Ananias
overview: Ananias was a male disciple located in Damascus who played a crucial role in caring for Saul, later known as Paul. Scripture identifies him specifically in Acts 9:10. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Ananias means 'YHWH is gracious' and is a proper name mentioned in Acts 9:10. This meaning reflects the gracious nature of God, though the name was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Ananias beyond his role as a disciple who cared for Saul/Paul. No other personal relationships are noted.
scriptureSignificance: Ananias is significant in the biblical narrative for his obedience and faith in ministering to Saul during a pivotal moment of Saul's conversion and calling as Paul. His willingness to care for Saul demonstrates the grace and provision of God in the early church, facilitating the transformation of a former persecutor into a devoted apostle.
